metadata.title: Grade 9 & 10 Foundation Ready-Reference Formulas & Exam Speed Hacks Handout
metadata.target_audience: Grade 9-10 Foundation, JEE Main, NEET (UG), and National Science Olympiad (NSEJS/IJSO)

universal_meta_heuristics.rule: Every additive term and both sides of an equality must possess identical SI dimensions [M^a L^b T^c].
universal_meta_heuristics.exam_application: Instantly eliminates 1 to 2 incorrect multiple-choice options before writing any physics derivation.

universal_meta_heuristics.rule: Test asymptotic parameter extremes (θ→0°, θ→90°, μ→0, μ→∞, m→0, M→∞).
universal_meta_heuristics.exam_application: If an acceleration formula on an incline does not yield a = g sinθ when μ→0, or a = g when θ→90°, reject it immediately.

universal_meta_heuristics.rule: Total ionic charges on the reactant side must strictly match total ionic charges on the product side (Σ q_initial = Σ q_final).
universal_meta_heuristics.exam_application: Validates redox equation balancing in 5 seconds without re-counting intermediate hydrogen and oxygen atoms.

universal_meta_heuristics.rule: In closed chemical reactions, total grams of reactants equal total grams of products (Σ m_reactants = Σ m_products).
universal_meta_heuristics.exam_application: Cracks complex multi-stage mixture and gas stoichiometry problems via global mass conservation.

sections.title: Galileo's Odd-Integer Free-Fall Law
sections.rationale: Over consecutive equal time intervals Δt from rest under constant acceleration a, distance s<sub>n</sub> = ½ a (Δt)² (2n - 1).
sections.speed_hack: Avoid quadratic displacement equations. If distance in the 1st second is h, distance in the 3rd second is identically 5h.
sections.boundary_condition: Initial velocity must be strictly zero (u = 0) and acceleration must be constant.
sections.trap_warning: Never apply if body has non-zero initial speed (u ≠ 0). In that case, s<sub>n</sub> = u Δt + ½ a (Δt)² (2n - 1).

drill.lightning_solution: Distance in 4th second for dropped stone = (2×4 - 1) × (½ g) = 7 × 4.9 = 34.3 m directly.

sections.title: Average Speed for Segmented Journeys
sections.formula: Equal Distances: v<sub>avg</sub> = 2 v<sub>1</sub> v<sub>2</sub> / (v<sub>1</sub> + v<sub>2</sub>)  |  Equal Times: v<sub>avg</sub> = (v<sub>1</sub> + v<sub>2</sub>) / 2
sections.rationale: Equal distances mandate harmonic mean (time varies inversely with speed); equal times mandate arithmetic mean.
sections.speed_hack: By AM-HM inequality, v<sub>avg, time</sub> ≥ v<sub>avg, dist</sub> with equality iff v<sub>1</sub> = v<sub>2</sub>.
sections.boundary_condition: Applicable strictly when motion occurs along a single straight direction without turning points.
sections.trap_warning: Round-trip journeys always have equal distances (use harmonic mean), not equal times.

drill.lightning_solution: Vehicle travels at 40 km/h and returns at 60 km/h: v<sub>avg</sub> = 2(40)(60)/(40 + 60) = 48 km/h (never 50 km/h!).

sections.title: Stopping Distance & Velocity Scaling Rule
sections.formula: d<sub>stop</sub> = v₀² / (2a)   ∝   v₀²,    t<sub>stop</sub> = v₀ / a   ∝   v₀
sections.rationale: From v² = u² - 2as, setting v = 0 gives stopping distance directly proportional to the square of initial speed.
sections.speed_hack: If speed is multiplied by factor k, stopping distance multiplies by k². Doubling speed (k=2) quadruples stopping distance (4×).
sections.boundary_condition: Braking acceleration a must remain constant throughout retardation.
sections.trap_warning: Stopping distance scales as v², but stopping time scales linearly as v. Never confuse the two exponents.

drill.lightning_solution: Car at 50 km/h stops in 12 m. At 150 km/h (3× speed), stopping distance = 12 × 3² = 12 × 9 = 108 m instantly.

sections.title: Freeze-Frame Relative Collision & Overtaking
sections.formula: v<sub>A/B</sub> = v<sub>A</sub> - v<sub>B</sub>,    a<sub>A/B</sub> = a<sub>A</sub> - a<sub>B</sub>,    s<sub>min</sub> = v<sub>rel</sub>² / (2 |a<sub>rel</sub>|)
sections.rationale: Transforming into target B's reference frame reduces a two-body coupled differential system into a single 1D stopping calculation.
sections.speed_hack: To prevent rear-end collision when vehicle A approaches vehicle B: minimum safe initial gap is s<sub>min</sub> = (v<sub>A</sub> - v<sub>B</sub>)² / (2 a<sub>decel</sub>).
sections.boundary_condition: Relative acceleration a<sub>rel</sub> must remain constant throughout the braking maneuver.
sections.trap_warning: In opposing motion (head-on), remember vector signs: v<sub>rel</sub> = v<sub>A</sub> - (-v<sub>B</sub>) = v<sub>A</sub> + v<sub>B</sub>.

drill.lightning_solution: Cars A (100 km/h) & B (80 km/h): passenger in B observes relative speed v<sub>rel</sub> = 100 - 80 = +20 km/h forward.

sections.title: The Factored Trajectory Equation
sections.formula: y = x tanθ (1 - x / R)
sections.rationale: Factoring x tanθ from the standard parabola y = x tanθ - [g x² / (2 v₀² cos²θ)] directly exposes horizontal range R = (v₀² sin 2θ) / g.
sections.speed_hack: When given barrier coordinates (x₁, y₁), never expand cos²θ. Use tanθ = y₁ / [x₁ (1 - x₁ / R)] for an instant 1-line solve.
sections.boundary_condition: Launch and landing points must be at the same vertical datum (level horizontal terrain).
sections.trap_warning: Do not use when launching onto an elevated terrace (elevation mismatch breaks level range symmetry).

drill.lightning_solution: Passes through (x=5m, y=1m) with range R=20m: 1 = 5 tanθ (1 - 5/20) = 5 tanθ (3/4) ⇒ tanθ = 4/15.

sections.title: Complementary Launch Angles Invariants
sections.formula: R<sub>θ</sub> = R<sub>90°-θ</sub>  |  R = 4 √(H<sub>1</sub> H<sub>2</sub>)  |  t<sub>1</sub> t<sub>2</sub> = 2R / g  |  H<sub>1</sub> + H<sub>2</sub> = v₀² / (2g)
sections.rationale: Angles θ and 90°-θ yield identical sin 2θ. Cross products of heights and times cancel trigonometric factors identically.
sections.speed_hack: Given maximum heights H₁ and H₂ of two complementary shots with identical speed, Range is 4√(H₁ H₂) without computing speed v₀ or angle θ.
sections.boundary_condition: Initial speeds must be identical, launched over horizontal ground.
sections.trap_warning: Remember factor 4 in R = 4√(H₁ H₂); forgetting factor 4 is the most common arithmetic trap.

sections.title: Horizontal Tower Launch & Free-Fall Decoupling
sections.formula: t<sub>fall</sub> = √(2h / g),    v<sub>x</sub> = R / √(2h / g),    v<sub>impact</sub> = √(v<sub>x</sub>² + 2gh)
sections.rationale: Vertical motion is pure free fall from rest independent of horizontal launch speed.
sections.speed_hack: For horizontal launch from height h, horizontal speed is directly v = R / t = R / √(2h / g).
sections.boundary_condition: Initial vertical velocity must be zero (purely horizontal takeoff).
sections.trap_warning: Do not treat landing distances as proportional to velocity if vertical fall heights differ.

drill.lightning_solution: h = 20m, lands at R = 40m. t = √(2(20)/10) = 2.0s ⇒ Horizontal launch speed v₀ = 40 / 2.0 = 20 m/s.

sections.title: Maximum Range & Apex Energy Invariants
sections.formula: At θ = 45°: R<sub>max</sub> = v₀² / g = 4 H<sub>max</sub>  |  K<sub>apex</sub> = K₀ cos²θ
sections.rationale: Maximum range occurs when sin 2θ = 1 (θ = 45°). Vertical velocity at apex vanishes; horizontal velocity v₀ cosθ remains invariant.
sections.speed_hack: At maximum range angle (45°), Range is always exactly 4 times the maximum height (R = 4H). Apex kinetic energy is exactly half (½ K₀).
sections.boundary_condition: Constant gravitational acceleration g without atmospheric air drag.
sections.trap_warning: Kinetic energy at highest point is not zero; it equals ½ m (v₀ cosθ)², which is non-zero for any oblique angle.

drill.lightning_solution: If kinetic energy at apex is half of initial KE: cos²θ = ½ ⇒ cosθ = 1/√2 ⇒ θ = 45° (Maximum range angle!).

modules.module_title: Newton's Laws, Friction Engine & Constraint Relations

sections.title: Whole-System Acceleration Heuristic
sections.formula: a<sub>sys</sub> = (Σ F<sub>driving</sub> - Σ F<sub>opposing</sub>) / Σ m<sub>inertial</sub>
sections.rationale: Internal constraint forces (tensions, mutual normal contact forces) form action-reaction pairs that cancel over the total free body.
sections.speed_hack: Never write simultaneous 3-variable equations for Atwood or connected incline systems. One line gives acceleration directly.
sections.boundary_condition: All interconnected components must share identical scalar acceleration magnitude along the constraint path.
sections.trap_warning: Include all moving masses in denominator, including pulleys if they have non-negligible rotational inertia.

drill.lightning_solution: Masses 3 kg & 2 kg over smooth pulley: a = (3 - 2)g / (3 + 2) = g / 5 = 2.0 m/s². Tension T = 2(3)(2)g / 5 = 24 N.

sections.title: Inclined Plane Friction & Time Ratio Scaling
sections.formula: a = g (sinθ - μ cosθ)  |  If t<sub>rough</sub> = n · t<sub>smooth</sub> ⇒ μ = tanθ [ 1 - (1 / n²) ]
sections.rationale: From s = ½ a t², acceleration varies inversely as t². Thus a_rough / a_smooth = 1 / n², yielding μ in one line.
sections.speed_hack: If a block takes n times longer to slide down a rough incline than a smooth incline of angle θ, μ = tanθ (1 - 1/n²) directly.
sections.boundary_condition: Incline angle θ must exceed the angle of repose (tanθ > μ) so that motion actually occurs from rest.
sections.trap_warning: Factor is (1 - 1/n²), never (1 - 1/n).

drill.lightning_solution: Takes twice as long (n=2) on 45° rough plane: μ = tan 45° [1 - 1/(2²)] = 1 × (1 - 1/4) = 0.75 in 5 seconds.

sections.title: Pulling vs. Pushing Friction Margin
sections.formula: N<sub>pull</sub> = mg - F sinθ  (f<sub>max</sub> = μ N<sub>pull</sub>)  |  N<sub>push</sub> = mg + F sinθ  (f<sub>max</sub> = μ N<sub>push</sub>)
sections.rationale: Pulling has an upward vertical component reducing normal force; pushing has a downward vertical component increasing normal force.
sections.speed_hack: Normal shift is exactly ΔN = 2 F sinθ. Pushing jams completely when tanθ = μ (force required blows up to infinity!).
sections.boundary_condition: Force applied at angle θ to horizontal on rough horizontal surface.
sections.trap_warning: If pulling force is very large (F sinθ > mg), the body lifts off the surface (N = 0, friction vanishes completely).

drill.lightning_solution: Pulling reduces normal force by F sinθ, decreasing friction resistance f = μ N. Pushing adds F sinθ, increasing resistance.

sections.title: Two-Block Slipping Threshold Rule
sections.formula: a<sub>max</sub> = μ<sub>s</sub> g,    F<sub>thresh</sub> = (M + m) μ<sub>s</sub> g
sections.rationale: Friction between the blocks is the sole force accelerating the upper block m; its maximum possible acceleration is μ_s g.
sections.speed_hack: Compute system acceleration a_sys = F / (M + m). If a_sys ≤ μ_s g, they move together without slip. If a_sys > μ_s g, slip occurs.
sections.boundary_condition: Smooth horizontal ground under lower block M; friction acts only at mutual interface.
sections.trap_warning: Once slipping begins, static friction μ_s must immediately be replaced by kinetic friction μ_k.

drill.lightning_solution: m=2kg on M=3kg, μ_s=0.4: a_max = 0.4(10) = 4 m/s². Maximum pulling force without slipping is F_thresh = (2 + 3)(4) = 20 N.

sections.title: Molarity-to-Molality Direct Conversion
sections.formula: m = 1000 M / (1000 d - M M<sub>w</sub>)    |    d = (M / 1000) [ (1000 / m) + M<sub>w</sub> ]
sections.rationale: In 1000 mL solution: total mass = 1000 d grams, solute mass = M M_w grams, solvent mass = (1000 d - M M_w) / 1000 kg.
sections.speed_hack: Eliminates the tedious 2-page 'Assume 1 L solution' algebra. Direct plug-and-chug with density d in g/mL.
sections.boundary_condition: Density d must be in g/mL (or g/cm³). Solute molar mass M_w in g/mol.
sections.trap_warning: Ensure d is in g/mL, not kg/m³. If given in kg/m³, divide by 1000 first.

sections.title: Alligation Cross for Binary Mixture Molar Mass
sections.formula: n₁ / n₂ = |M₂ - M_avg| / |M₁ - M_avg|
sections.rationale: M_avg = (n₁ M₁ + n₂ M₂) / (n₁ + n₂) rearranged gives n₁ (M_avg - M₁) = n₂ (M₂ - M_avg).
sections.speed_hack: Solves isotope natural abundances, binary alloy compositions, and gas mixture ratios in 5 seconds via cross subtraction.
sections.boundary_condition: Applies strictly to binary (two-component) mixtures.
sections.trap_warning: Alligation gives mole ratio for molar properties, but mass ratio for mass-specific properties (like mass percentages).

drill.lightning_solution: 7g N₂ (0.25 mol) & 8g Ar (0.20 mol): n_ratio = 5:4. Mole fraction of Ar = 4/9. Partial pressure P_Ar = (4/9)(27 bar) = 12 bar.

sections.title: Faraday's Electrolysis Direct Electron Factor
sections.formula: 1 Faraday = 96,500 C ≡ 1 mole of electrons  |  Mass m = (M / z) (Q / F)
sections.rationale: Reduction of 1 mole of M^(z+) requires exactly z moles of electrons (z Faradays of charge).
sections.speed_hack: Never use complex electrochemical equivalent formulas. Simply use: Moles deposited = Faradays / z.
sections.boundary_condition: 100% current efficiency assumed unless specified otherwise.
sections.trap_warning: Identify cation charge z carefully: e.g., Cu²+ has z=2, but Cu+ (cuprous) has z=1.

drill.lightning_solution: Ca²+ + 2e⁻ → Ca. Molar mass Ca = 40 g/mol ⇒ 40g requires 2 F. Therefore 20g requires exactly 1.0 F.

sections.title: Limiting Reagent Dimensionless Ratio Test
sections.formula: R<sub>i</sub> = n<sub>i</sub> / ν<sub>i</sub>    (ν<sub>i</sub> = stoichiometric coefficient)
sections.rationale: Reaction progress is bounded by the reactant with the minimum value of moles divided by its stoichiometric number.
sections.speed_hack: Divide initial moles of each reactant by its balanced coefficient. Smallest ratio is strictly the Limiting Reagent (LR).
sections.boundary_condition: Reaction must go to completion (irreversible stoichiometry).
sections.trap_warning: Never compare raw masses or raw moles directly; always divide by stoichiometric coefficients first.

drill.lightning_solution: N₂ + 3 H₂ → 2 NH₃ with 2 mol N₂ and 3 mol H₂. R_N = 2/1 = 2; R_H = 3/3 = 1. H₂ is LR (ratio 1 < 2), yielding 2 mol NH₃.

modules.module_title: Redox Mastery, n-Factor Matrix & Rapid Titrations

sections.title: The 'BAN' Mnemonic for Permanganate (KMnO₄)
sections.formula: Basic (strongly alkaline): n = 1  |  Acidic: n = 5  |  Neutral / weakly basic: n = 3
sections.rationale: Acidic: MnO₄⁻ + 5e⁻ → Mn²⁺ (+7→+2). Neutral: MnO₄⁻ + 3e⁻ → MnO₂ (+7→+4). Strongly Basic: MnO₄⁻ + 1e⁻ → MnO₄²⁻ (+7→+6).
sections.speed_hack: Remember keyword 'BAN 1-5-3' (Basic=1, Acidic=5, Neutral=3) to instantly write equivalent weights without balancing half-cells.
sections.boundary_condition: Acidic medium must use dilute H₂SO₄, never concentrated HCl (which oxidizes Cl⁻ to Cl₂).
sections.trap_warning: In neutral or faintly alkaline medium, n = 3 (forms MnO₂), not n = 5.

drill.lightning_solution: Equivalent weight of KMnO₄ in acid is M/5; in neutral medium (forming MnO₂) it is M/3; in strongly basic medium it is M/1.

sections.title: Dichromate Acidic Invariant
sections.formula: Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 14H⁺ + 6e⁻ → 2Cr³⁺ + 7H₂O    (n = 2 × |6 - 3| = 6)
sections.rationale: Two chromium atoms per formula unit each undergo a 3-electron reduction from +6 to +3.
sections.speed_hack: Equivalent weight of K₂Cr₂O₇ in acidic medium is always strictly M / 6.
sections.boundary_condition: Operates as an oxidant in acidic solution; in alkaline medium it hydrolyzes to yellow chromate CrO₄²⁻.
sections.trap_warning: Multiply change in oxidation state per atom (3) by number of Cr atoms in formula unit (2) = 6. Forgetting factor 2 is fatal.

drill.lightning_solution: Complete reduction of 1 mol K₂Cr₂O₇ to Cr³⁺ in acidic medium consumes exactly 6 Faradays (6 × 96,500 C) of charge.

sections.title: Parallel Resistor Rule for Disproportionation
sections.formula: n<sub>eq</sub> = (n<sub>ox</sub> · n<sub>red</sub>) / (n<sub>ox</sub> + n<sub>red</sub>)    ⇔    1 / n<sub>eq</sub> = 1 / n<sub>ox</sub> + 1 / n<sub>red</sub>
sections.rationale: Conserving electrons across simultaneously oxidized and reduced branches yields equivalent weight E = M (1/n_ox + 1/n_red).
sections.speed_hack: Identical structure to parallel resistors. Disproportionation n-factor is computed in 5 seconds without writing full balanced stoichiometry.
sections.boundary_condition: Applicable strictly when a single reactant disproportionates into two distinct redox products.
sections.trap_warning: Do not simply add n_ox + n_red; addition is only valid when two different elements in the same compound both oxidize.

drill.lightning_solution: Cl₂ + 2 OH⁻ → Cl⁻ (n_red = 1) + ClO⁻ (n_ox = 1). n_eq = (1×1)/(1+1) = 0.5. Equivalent weight of Cl₂ is M / 0.5 = 2M.

sections.title: The Golden Law of Equivalents (Titration Shortcut)
sections.formula: (N₁ V₁)<sub>oxidant</sub> = (N₂ V₂)<sub>reductant</sub>    ⇔    n₁ · moles₁ = n₂ · moles₂
sections.rationale: One equivalent of any oxidizing agent completely consumes exactly one equivalent of any reducing agent.
sections.speed_hack: Never balance full complex redox equations during exam conditions. Multiply moles by respective n-factors and equate directly.
sections.boundary_condition: All reactants must react completely without side reactions.
sections.trap_warning: In FeC₂O₄ (ferrous oxalate), both Fe²⁺ (1e⁻) and C₂O₄²⁻ (2e⁻) oxidize, so n-factor is 1 + 2 = 3!

drill.lightning_solution: Oxalic acid (H₂C₂O₄, n=2) titrated with acidified KMnO₄ (n=5): 2 × moles_ox = 5 × moles_perm ⇒ 5 mol oxalic acid requires 2 mol KMnO₄.
